payload.report: The patient's irregularly linear atrophic plaque on the right shoulder, arborizing purple areas, easy bruising, and prior ipsilateral shoulder replacement are consistent with intralymphatic histiocytosis. The biopsy showing dense CD68+ histiocytic infiltrate within D2-40-positive lymphatic vessels and lacking sclerotic collagen is the characteristic diagnostic finding. This directly excludes linear morphea/scleroderma and post-surgical/trauma fibrosis, and makes malignant infiltration and low-flow vascular malformation unlikely. Langerhans cell histiocytosis remains a low residual possibility pending autoimmune serology and S100/CD1a/factor XIIIa immunohistochemistry, but the already-diagnostic histiocytic infiltrate establishes intralymphatic histiocytosis. The frontier is sufficiently refined, so no further hypotheses are needed.
